Hi all — quick note from the solutions side. We have a compact dashboard bundle that covers token consumption by route, 95/99/99.9 latency percentiles, and error taxonomy panels (model errors, infra timeouts, validation). I attached a markdown runbook draft that follows your template and includes alert thresholds we typically recommend.

Tracing hooks: we recommend two insertion points: (1) ingress handler — attach request metadata (customer_id, route, prompt_size) and start a root span; (2) model-invoke path — create child spans for pre-processing, model call, post-processing and include token counts in span tags. For lower-cost paths (background batch jobs) you can sample at 1-5% and keep full traces for high-latency tails.

I'll share the Grafana JSON export in the Drive link Soojin added and include a short checklist for instrumenting headers and sampling.

Attachments: obs-runbook-v1.md (md)

Alex — quick answers after reviewing the draft and our standard playbook: 
- Alert routing: model-invoke latency breach (>=2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1-min windows) -> P1 (page on-call, page rotation: infra-sre). P2 (error rate > 5% for 5 minutes) -> email + Slack #sre-alerts. P3 (dashboard thresholds drift) -> Slack -> owner. We'll include explicit escalation steps in the runbook.
- Span tags: use "customer.id" and "request.type" as canonical keys; include "prompt.tokens" and "model.variant" as optional tags. That maps cleanly to our tracing dashboards.

I've attached a simple alert-routing diagram and updated the runbook checklist in Drive. I'll speak to our infra SRE before the walkthrough so we can show a quick demo of traces+alerts.

Attachments: alert-routing-diagram.png (png)

Best,
Jonas Weber
Implementation Lead, Redwood Inference
